result.title: Diagnosing Personalization Failures in Mobile GUI Agents
result.summary: Unlike conventional GUI agents, personalized GUI agents require user preferences to guide sequential execution over changing GUI states. This raises two challenges: determining HOW each preference should alter execution strategy and WHEN it should take effect along the interaction trajectory. Existing benchmarks primarily evaluate overall task success, offering limited insight into these questions. We introduce PrefDiag-Bench with two components: (1) a categorization of preferences into five types, characterizing HOW they affect execution; and (2) a stage-wise diagnostic framework with 1,664 probes, tracing WHEN preferences should take effect and where failures occur. We evaluate eleven GUI agent systems, including end-to-end agents and agentic workflows, under two forms of user context: explicit user profiles and behavioral memory logs. Although existing agents achieve relatively high completion rates on non-personalized tasks, performance is substantially lower on preference-personalized tasks. Even the best-performing model, Seed-2.0-Pro, achieves only 47.17% on Process preferences under explicit user profiles. Agents struggle particularly with Ranking and Process preferences. Further analysis reveals two key capability bottlenecks: selecting relevant evidence from user history and recognizing when preferences should take effect during execution. Controlled interventions that explicitly provide relevant evidence improve end-to-end task success by up to 7.06%. PrefDiag-Bench offers a more systematic evaluation of GUI agents' personalization capabilities beyond overall task success. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Zhixin-L/PrefDiag-Bench.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PrefDiag-Bench，将个性化偏好分为五类，并用 1,664 个分阶段探针诊断 11 个移动 GUI agent 在显式用户画像与行为记忆日志下的执行失败，发现主要瓶颈是筛选相关历史证据与判断偏好何时生效。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分阶段诊断「证据何时应介入、何时失效」的思路，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 STOP/介入时机的评价提供参照，但未涉及 latent 状态或推理机制，需核查可迁移性。
